- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from peak forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model tends to continue falling; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 3–5 days by 2–5% to align with observed lag.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-forecast, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drop.
